Chapter 02 of 18

The Morning Mist

AssembleCitywide80 BPM
The story

When the meeting ends, something has to carry the decision out into the city. That job belongs to the Morning Mist. A light mist, or a thin rain, follows the meeting out of Trout Lake and drifts over every district before sunrise. It carries the meeting's mood the way weather carries a smell. Nobody reads it, but everybody receives it.

The mist does not care about walls. It slips in through vents and open windows and comes home on wet footprints. It settles on the wires before the Wire Choir wakes, and the crows fly through it on their way to work and take the day's tone from it. When it moves on, the city is slightly better tuned than it was before.

Some streets miss it. If your street is dry at dawn, it did not get the message, and it will run yesterday's version of the day until the Repair People notice and fix it. Terminal Fog is the mist's late-night relative, and it does the opposite job. The mist delivers the day. The fog takes it away.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
